nuance: 가격 is the neutral word for the listed price of a thing in stores. In casual speech people often just ask 얼마예요 instead of using the word 가격.
mistakes: Confusing 가격 with 값, though both mean price

examples: This bag is on discount today.
The discount is really big and nice.
nuance: 할인 means a price reduction and pairs with 되다 to say something is discounted. To ask for one yourself you say 할인 돼요 rather than the English word sale.
mistakes: Saying 할인해요 to a clerk when you mean please discount

examples: I have little cash right now.
nuance: 현금 means physical paper money and coins as opposed to a card. The means particle 으로 is used to say you pay with it, as in 현금으로.
mistakes: Using 에 instead of 으로 to say pay with cash

examples: There are many coins in my wallet.
I pay the bus fare with coins.
nuance: 동전 means metal coins, while paper money is called 지폐. Together they make up 현금, so do not use 동전 for bills.
mistakes: Calling paper money 동전 instead of 지폐

examples: My wallet is inside the bag.
I left my wallet at home.
nuance: 지갑 means a wallet or purse that holds money and cards. A larger handbag is 가방, so keep the small money holder separate.
mistakes: Confusing 지갑 the wallet with 가방 the bag

usage: I put it in the bag
examples: Please put it in one bag.
nuance: 봉투 means a flat paper or plastic bag and also an envelope for letters or money. At a store it is the shopping bag they give for your items.
mistakes: Using 봉투 for a backpack instead of 가방

examples: Please go to that checkout to pay.
There are many people at the checkout.
nuance: 계산대 means the counter where you pay in a store or supermarket. The direction particle 으로 is natural for heading toward it, as in 계산대로.
mistakes: Confusing 계산대 the counter with 계산 the act of paying

examples: There are many customers in the shop today.
nuance: 손님 means a customer in a shop and also a guest visiting your home. The polite counter 분 is used for counting them, as in 손님 한 분.
mistakes: Using 사람 instead of the polite 손님 for customers

examples: This shop clerk is very kind.
I asked the clerk the price.
The clerk gave me a bag.
nuance: 점원 means a salesclerk who works in a shop and helps customers. To address one politely Koreans often say 저기요 rather than calling them 점원.
mistakes: Confusing 점원 the clerk with 손님 the customer

examples: The department store has a sale this week.
I bought clothes during the sale.
nuance: 세일 is a borrowed word for a store-wide sale event and pairs with 하다 as 세일을 해요. For a discount on one item Koreans more often say 할인.
mistakes: Mixing up 세일 the event with 할인 a single discount

examples: Can I get a refund here?
A refund is possible with a receipt.
nuance: 환불 means getting your money back for a returned item. To ask for one you say 환불해 주세요, and to exchange instead you say 교환.
mistakes: Confusing 환불 a money refund with 교환 an exchange

examples: I put the receipt in my wallet.
nuance: 영수증 means the printed receipt proving you paid for something. Clerks often ask 영수증 드릴까요 to check if you want one before printing it.
mistakes: Confusing 영수증 the receipt with 계산서 the bill
